_about: Step 1 test: can the image model paint pieces that cut cleanly off the board, fit back together, and keep one look across samples and poses? 7 images at 2K.
style: Style: children's picture-book art made entirely of cut pieces of hand-painted tissue paper. Inside each piece: bold acrylic brush streaks, sponge mottling and comb-scraped texture in a few rich colours. Crisp scissor-cut edges. Flat, layered collage with no 3D shading and no outlines. Everything sits on a plain, flat, evenly lit cream paper board that fills the whole image. No cast shadows, no frame, no text, no letters, no numbers.

assets.prompt: A single small bird from the Chinese myth of Jingwei: crow-sized, with a dark indigo-black body, a patterned head, a white beak and bright red feet. Side view facing right, wings spread in flight, the whole bird visible. The bird is isolated in the middle of the board with a wide empty margin of board on every side.

The attached image is a cut-paper bird. Make its puppet parts sheet: the same bird taken apart into separate flat cut-paper pieces, laid out on the board like parts before assembly. Pieces: the body with head and beak (no wings, no tail, no legs), the near wing, the far wing, the tail, and the two legs with feet. Keep every piece's colours, paints and brush textures exactly as in the attached bird. Every piece is complete and whole, nothing overlaps, and plain board shows between all pieces with clear gaps. Leave a wide empty margin of board around the edges.
